title: GPUParticles3D sub-emitter AT_START: first emission after inactivity does not spawns sub-particles
body: ### Tested versions Found and reproducible in v4.5.1.stable.mono.official [f62fdbde1] (at time of writing also reproducible on latest master branch [caf1670](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/caf16709af9f08bb430ddb8cffc10cbf66c62437)) ### System information Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - macOS Tahoe (26.4.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 Pro (Apple9) - Apple M4 Pro (14 threads) - 48.00 GiB memory ### Issue description When using GPU particles with a sub-emitter in AT_START mode and emitting via EmitParticle(), the first emission after the particle system goes inactive never spawns sub-emitter particles. Subsequent emissions within the same lifetime window work correctly. The first emission should also spawn sub-emitter particles. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68b7f2a4-e18f-4cb7-9d7a-1fbcb8b8e52f ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a GPUParticles3D* (parent-emitter) with a ParticleProcessMaterial with sub_emitter_mode = AT_START 2. Add another GPUParticles3D* (sub-emitter) and assign it as the parent's sub-emitter 3. Call EmitParticle() on parent-emitter -> sub-emitter particles are missing 4. Call EmitParticle() again within the lifetime -> sub-emitter particles appear 5. Wait for the system to go inactive. 6. repeat from step 3. *The bug is reproducible using fixed FPS, but not consistently reproducible. Set `GPUParticles3D.Time.FPS = 0` to reproduce consistently. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [ParticlesTestProject.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26861183/ParticlesTestProject.zip)
